name: VeloSearch
target_user: Data engineers and systems architects building lightweight local search solutions.
problem: Standard vector databases are heavy and lack integrated lexical search, while traditional search engines require complex external services and fail to provide hybrid retrieval without substantial overhead.
pain: High latency, complex deployment setups, excessive memory bloat, and mismatched search results when trying to combine semantic vector search with exact keyword matching on local systems.
solution: A zero-dependency hybrid vector-lexical search engine written in Python 3.12. It features a custom BM25 index, a custom Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH) dense vector index, and a Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) engine to combine semantic and keyword results.
verification: Deterministic tests verifying index consistency under concurrency, zero-vector search queries, malformed text inputs, and exact RRF rank merging order using seeded random projections.
major_features: Inverted index builder with positional postings lists for phrase matching
Custom English Porter Stemmer and tokenizer implementing word normalization
Sparse BM25 scoring engine calculating term frequency and inverse document frequency
Dense vector index using Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH) for high-dimensional cosine similarity
Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) rank merger with configurable hyper-parameters
On-disk binary serialization layout with CRC32 integrity verification
Boolean query parser supporting nested AND, OR, and NOT operators
Dynamic document update and deletion mechanics updating both sparse and dense indexes in-place
truth_policy: Only validated behavior may be claimed as working.
